sentences.en: He's absolutely gutted.
sentences.zh: 他彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: He wanted to stay in Brazil because basically in Brazil, he's got everything as kind of as he wants it.
sentences.zh: 他想留在巴西，因为基本上在巴西，他拥有他想要的一切。

sentences.en: If he goes back to Europe, it's the home of revolution.
sentences.zh: 如果他回到欧洲，那里是革命的温床。

sentences.en: Europe is the home of political ferment and turbulence.
sentences.zh: 欧洲是政治动荡和骚乱的中心。

sentences.en: And, you know, he'll be pushed around by all these Portuguese bigwigs.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他会被所有这些葡萄牙大人物摆布。

sentences.en: He doesn't want that.
sentences.zh: 他不想要那样。

sentences.en: He's so sad, apparently, that he can't speak.
sentences.zh: 据说他难过得说不出话来。

sentences.en: But before he's lost the ability to speak, he says to his son, Pedro, you stay in Brazil as regent in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 但在他失去说话能力之前，他对他儿子佩德罗说，你留在巴西担任巴西摄政王。

sentences.en: And basically, if they tell you to come back, if they try to take Brazil from you, you should
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果他们叫你回去，如果他们试图从你手中夺走巴西，你应该

sentences.en: declare independence or something.
sentences.zh: 宣布独立或者什么的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's completely upfront about this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对此完全直言不讳。

sentences.en: Zhao comes back.
sentences.zh: 若昂六世回来了。

sentences.en: The Portuguese browbeat him into this new constitution.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人强迫他接受了这部新宪法。

sentences.en: He has to swear an oath of loyalty to the constitution.
sentences.zh: 他必须宣誓效忠宪法。

sentences.en: His wife refuses, so she's kind of stripped of her royal privileges.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子拒绝了，所以她被剥夺了王室特权。

sentences.en: But now the Portuguese go further and they say, your son is still in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 但现在葡萄牙人更进一步，他们说，你儿子还在巴西。

sentences.en: He needs to come back to Portugal as well.
sentences.zh: 他也需要回到葡萄牙。

sentences.en: And this business of him being regent in Brazil is rubbish.
sentences.zh: 他担任巴西摄政王这事儿简直是胡闹。

sentences.en: You know, we're the, yeah, he needs to scrap all that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是，是的，他需要废除这一切。

sentences.en: The Brazilian masons, actually, are very anti this.
sentences.zh: 巴西的共济会成员实际上非常反对这一点。

sentences.en: And they say, no, no, no, they invest him in Brazil with the title Defender of Brazil,
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，不，不，他们在巴西授予他“巴西守护者”的头衔，

sentences.en: Don Pedro.
sentences.zh: 唐·佩德罗。

sentences.en: Don Pedro is a slightly useless man as well.
sentences.zh: 唐·佩德罗也是个稍微有点没用的人。

sentences.en: He's been very highly educated, but he's, everybody says he can't focus.
sentences.zh: 他受过非常良好的教育，但每个人都说他无法集中注意力。

sentences.en: He's always having affairs with people.
sentences.zh: 他总是和人有风流韵事。

sentences.en: He's sort of badly behaved.
sentences.zh: 他表现得很糟糕。

sentences.en: And it basically all comes to a head in the late summer of 1822.
sentences.zh: 这一切基本上在1822年夏末达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: The Portuguese say, you know, this is an absolute ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人说，你知道，这是最后的通牒。

sentences.en: You have, Pedro has to come back to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 你必须，佩德罗必须回到葡萄牙。

sentences.en: Pedro, unfortunately, has chronic diarrhea.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，佩德罗患有慢性腹泻。

sentences.en: So he's not cutting a very glamorous figure.
sentences.zh: 所以他的形象不太光彩。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, he gives this rousing speech in between sort of running to the loo.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，他在跑去厕所的间隙发表了这番激昂的演讲。

sentences.en: Rushing off to the toilet.
sentences.zh: 冲向厕所。

sentences.en: In which he says, independence or death and all this, which is generally what?
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中说，不独立毋宁死之类的，这通常是？

sentences.en: Oh, Tom, I can't believe you did a sound effect on the, your first sound effect on the rest of history.
sentences.zh: 噢，汤姆，我不敢相信你在《历史的其余部分》中第一次使用了音效。

sentences.en: Well, first time for everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，凡事都有第一次。

sentences.en: And what a one to do.
sentences.zh: 而且还是这么一个音效。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he gives the speech.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他发表了演讲。

sentences.en: He says independence or death, which I think that all Latin American people say when they're declaring independence.
sentences.zh: 他说不独立毋宁死，我想所有拉丁美洲人在宣布独立时都会这么说。

sentences.en: I think that's the law, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想那是法律，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, by UN convention.
sentences.zh: 是的，根据联合国公约。

sentences.en: You have to say independence or death.
sentences.zh: 你必须说不独立毋宁死。

sentences.en: And they get independence because, of course, there's not really anything the Portuguese can do about it.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了独立，因为当然，葡萄牙人对此真的无能为力。

sentences.en: Yeah, so they can't do anything.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他们什么也做不了。

sentences.en: No, they haven't got, it's not like they've got a navy and an army that they can really use to crush the Brazilians.
sentences.zh: 不，他们没有，他们并没有一支真正能用来镇压巴西人的海军和军队。

sentences.en: What's the attitude of the British to this?
sentences.zh: 英国人对此的态度是什么？

sentences.en: Because presumably their attitude really matters because they control the shipping lanes that enable Portugal and Brazil to communicate with each other.
sentences.zh: 因为据推测他们的态度真的很重要，因为他们控制着使葡萄牙和巴西能够相互沟通的航道。

sentences.en: So really the British, the British actors, mediators, and the British don't care whether the Portuguese run Brazil or not.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上英国人，英国人充当调解人，而且英国人不在乎是否由葡萄牙人管理巴西。

sentences.en: What they want to do is to ensure their own commercial dominance in both places.
sentences.zh: 他们想要做的是确保他们在两地都有商业主导地位。

sentences.en: So they can sell all their woolen blankets and their corsets and ice skates.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以卖掉他们所有的羊毛毯、紧身胸衣和溜冰鞋。

sentences.en: But interestingly, for people who think that the British have not always behaved with distinction in the course of this, today's podcast,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，对于那些认为英国人在这个过程中表现得并不总是那么高尚的人来说，今天的播客，

sentences.en: one of the sort of quid pro quos for the British agreeing that they will, I mean, the British basically mediate and they persuade the Portuguese to give Brazil their independence,
sentences.zh: 英国人同意的交换条件之一，我的意思是，英国人基本上进行调解并说服葡萄牙人给予巴西独立，

sentences.en: to recognize Brazilian independence.
sentences.zh: 承认巴西独立。

sentences.en: One of the quid pro quos is that the British, this is the heyday really, I mean, abolitionism in Britain, the early 19th century.
sentences.zh: 交换条件之一是英国人，这确实是鼎盛时期，我的意思是，英国的废奴主义，19世纪初。

sentences.en: And they say, we want you to scrap slave trafficking, not necessarily abolish slavery within Brazil, but stop the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们希望你们废除奴隶贩卖，不一定是在巴西国内废除奴隶制，但要停止奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: And the Brazilians, in a sort of very roundabout way, they kind of agree.
sentences.zh: 而巴西人，以一种非常迂回的方式，算是同意了。

sentences.en: So in 1831, they agreed to a law that says basically when slaves arrive in Brazil, they will be considered free.
sentences.zh: 所以在1831年，他们同意了一项法律，基本上规定奴隶抵达巴西时，将被视为自由人。

sentences.en: And they completely and utterly ignore it.
sentences.zh: 但他们完全彻底地无视了它。

sentences.en: So it's a complete fiction and a fraud.
sentences.zh: 所以这完全是虚构和欺诈。

sentences.en: And is there a famous Portuguese phrase that sums us up?
sentences.zh: 有没有一句著名的葡萄牙语短语能概括这种情况？

sentences.en: Tom, you're reading the notes.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你在看笔记。

sentences.en: You're reading ahead.
sentences.zh: 你在提前看内容。

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: It's uma lei para inglês ver, a law for the British to see, which basically in Brazilian Portuguese means dressing it up.
sentences.zh: 那就是“uma lei para inglês ver”，意为“给英国人看的法律”，在巴西葡萄牙语中基本就是指做做样子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And actually, it's not until 1888 that slavery is abolished in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 事实上，直到1888年巴西才废除奴隶制。

sentences.en: And since I know we're running out of time, so I will just say this is Brazil.
sentences.zh: 既然我知道时间不多了，我只想说这就是巴西。

sentences.en: Brazil now vanishes from Portuguese history because it's on its own.
sentences.zh: 巴西从此从葡萄牙历史中消失了，因为它独立了。

sentences.en: But, Tom, we will be returning to Brazil, which is a country whose history is almost entirely unknown, certainly in Britain,
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，我们会回到巴西，这是一个历史几乎完全不为人知的国家，至少在英国是这样，

sentences.en: but probably in the English-speaking world more generally.
sentences.zh: 而且在整个英语世界可能也是如此。

sentences.en: We'll be returning to what happens to Brazil because Brazil obviously becomes an empire under Don Pedro and his successors.
sentences.zh: 我们将回到巴西后来发生的事情，因为巴西显然在唐·佩德罗及其继任者的统治下成为了一个帝国。

sentences.en: So we'll be returning to the Brazilian empire and the abolition of slavery in Brazil and the downfall of the Brazilian empire in a future podcast, won't we?
sentences.zh: 所以我们会在未来的播客中回到巴西帝国、巴西奴隶制的废除以及巴西帝国的衰落，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we're going to be doing some very exciting podcasts in the autumn.
sentences.zh: 因为我们秋季会有一些非常令人兴奋的播客节目。

sentences.en: Yes, we've got a part of a massive, very, very exciting plan that we've got coming.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们有一个宏大且非常、非常令人兴奋的计划即将推出。

sentences.zh: 最高机密。

sentences.zh: 但没错，我希望这绝对是值得期待的事情。

sentences.en: Okay, so I think we should stop at this point.
sentences.zh: 好了，我想我们应该在这里停一下。

sentences.zh: 我们现在已经为我们史诗般的葡萄牙历史系列的第四部分，也就是最后一部分做好了准备。

sentences.zh: 绝对的高潮。

sentences.zh: 我知道，多米尼克，这是你一直非常期待的一集，因为你是法朵音乐的超级粉丝，对吧？

sentences.zh: 独裁者。

sentences.zh: 所以托尔金，托尔金的《指环王》三部曲只有三部，汤姆，但我们更胜一筹，因为我们在这个宏大的系列中做了四部。

sentences.zh: 人们已经开始称其为历史播客界的《指环王》了，不是吗？
